source: NCERT Class XII, India — People and Economy, Ch. 1 (Population: Distribution, Density, Growth and Composition).

sections.heading: 1. Distribution and Density
points: India is the **second most populous country** (now the most populous); ~17.5% of world population on ~2.4% of land.
Distribution is **uneven**: **Uttar Pradesh** = most populous state; the northern plains and coastal areas are densely populated; hills/deserts sparsely.
**Population density** = persons per sq km (2011: ~382); highest in **Bihar**, lowest in **Arunachal Pradesh**.

sections.heading: 2. Population Growth
points: **Growth of population** = the change in numbers over a decade (Census every 10 years).
Phases: **1901–1921 stagnant** (1921 = 'Year of the Great Divide'); **1921–1951 steady**; **1951–1981 rapid ('population explosion')**; **1981 onwards** high but slowing.
Growth = **natural increase (births − deaths) + migration**; declining birth rate now.

sections.heading: 3. Population Composition
points: **Rural-urban:** most Indians still live in **rural areas** (~68%), but urbanisation is rising.
**Sex ratio** (females per 1000 males) = 943 (2011); **Kerala** highest, **Haryana** lowest (a concern).
**Age structure:** a **large young/working-age population** → **'demographic dividend'** potential.
**Linguistic and religious composition** — great diversity.

sections.heading: 4. Adolescents and Population Policy
points: **Adolescents (10–19)** are a large group needing health, education and nutrition.
**National Population Policy (2000)** aims to stabilise population, promote family planning, health and education.
Rising literacy and falling fertility reflect progress.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Uttar Pradesh = most populous state; Bihar = highest density; Arunachal = lowest.
1921 = 'Year of the Great Divide'; 1951–1981 = population explosion.
Sex ratio (2011) = 943; Kerala highest, Haryana lowest.
Most Indians live in rural areas (~68%); large working-age population = demographic dividend.
National Population Policy = 2000.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Uttar Pradesh** is the most populous state; **Bihar** has the highest density.
**1921 = Year of the Great Divide** in India's demographic history.
**Kerala** has the highest sex ratio; **Haryana** among the lowest.
The **National Population Policy** was adopted in **2000**.
